title: Switch it on properly
desc: The master switch, How things stand on Overview, and the first configuration that actually catches something.
learningGoal: After this lesson you can switch the Privacy Shield on for your organisation, read Overview's How things stand as a summary of your own decisions, and say what an empty category list and a missing detection service each really do.

steps.title: One policy, every chat in the organisation
steps.bodyMd:
Sooner or later somebody asks you to put it in writing: what personal data leaves this building when our people use AI?

At Van Dijk Groep, a Dutch SME of forty-odd people, purchasing pastes supplier contracts into chat, HR runs an automation over re-integration files, sales drafts proposals from a CRM export. All of it reaches an AI model unless somebody decides otherwise.

The Privacy Shield is that decision, made once for the whole organisation instead of left to each colleague. You find it under **Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield**; the page is headed *Organization Privacy Shield*.

Overview states the rule that matters most, in one line below its step cards: *Agents can be stricter, never looser.* These rules run before any rules on an individual agent, and if the two disagree, the stricter one wins.

steps.title: The master switch, and the steps it unlocks
steps.bodyMd:
Everything starts on the **Overview** tab with one switch: **Protect personal data** — *"Applies to every chat and every agent in this organisation. Off means nothing is checked, at all."* A new organisation has it **off**.

While it is off the page says so plainly: messages go to the AI unchanged, and the other steps stay inactive. Those are the four numbered steps on the path across the top — **1 What we look for**, **2 Your own data**, **3 When we find something**, **4 Leaving your org**. Overview and **What happened** stay readable.

Flip it and the steps wake up. Nothing you change anywhere on the page counts until you press **Save changes** in the bar at the bottom and see *Saved successfully!*

The switch is reversible. One consequence is not: documents already redacted when they were added to a knowledge base keep the redacted text.

steps.title: Read How things stand, not your memory
steps.bodyMd:
With the shield on, Overview becomes a read-only summary of every decision you made. Read this page, not your memory, before you tell anyone the shield is configured.

On top sits a review card — *"1 thing to review"*, *"3 things to review"* — listing the settings worth a second look, each with a link to the step that owns it. The number depends on your own settings; an optional safeguard that is off counts too.

Below it, **How things stand** shows one card per step, *in the order a message passes through*:

- **What we look for** — **Kinds of data** (*"n of 21"*) and **How strict**: Low sensitivity, Balanced, High sensitivity or Custom
- **Your own data** — your own types
- **When we find something** — the **Action**, plus **Automations** and **Knowledge bases**: Covered or Not covered
- **Leaving your org** — **Held back from tools** and **Last check**, which stays Off until you switch it on

Each card has a **Change** link to its step.

steps.question: Van Dijk Groep's admin switches Protect personal data on, presses Save changes, and ticks no categories at all. What happens to the next message containing a customer name and an IBAN?

choices.label: Both are found. An empty selection narrows nothing, so every kind stays in scope, and the default action stops the message.
Nothing is found, so the message reaches the AI unchanged.
choices.feedback: The review card on Overview reads that way — "nothing will ever be found" — but an empty list means "no narrowing", not "nothing to look for". Ticking categories narrows the scan; ticking none leaves it at its widest.

choices.label: The message goes through, because no action can fire until at least one category is ticked.
choices.feedback: The action fires on whatever the detector returns, and with no selection it is asked about all 21 kinds. Do not send the message is the default action, so a message like this one is stopped.

choices.label: Only the customer name is found; bank details have to be ticked before they are looked for.
choices.feedback: No category is special. Either your selection narrows the scan, for every category alike, or it is empty and nothing is narrowed.

steps.explanation: Ticking categories narrows what the detector is asked about; an empty list narrows nothing, so all 21 kinds stay in scope. Overview still flags it: the review card lists "No kinds of data are selected", and the What we look for card shows Kinds of data at "0 of 21" in amber. Read that as "nobody has made this decision yet" and make it deliberately, because that selection is what your tool rules and your evidence are built on later.

steps.title: Where the looking actually happens
steps.bodyMd:
The tick boxes describe what to look for. A separate detection service, running on your own server, does the looking: it reads each message before it goes to the AI, and that scan never leaves your own machines.

If the service was never installed, detection is simply off. Every kind ticked on **What we look for** has no effect and messages go through unchecked. Lists of words and fixed formats you added under **Your own data** still match, because exact words and patterns need no model.

steps.title: Installed, but not answering
steps.bodyMd:
The other failure is louder. When the service is installed but not responding, the shield refuses to guess: people read *"Privacy protection is temporarily unavailable, so your message was not sent."*

The Privacy Shield page tells you both states. The pill in its header turns red — *Detection service not installed* or *Detection service not responding* — where it normally reads *Detection running*. And Overview puts it first on the review card, *"The detection service is not responding"*, with a **Diagnose** button.

Fixing it is not yours, and the difference in route is the point. Everything you configure sits under **Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield** — your own organisation's area. The detection service belongs to whoever runs the server, so Diagnose opens the separate server-operator console: **Admin → Security → Guardrails**, which exists on Enterprise installs only. A platform admin installs or restarts the service there.

Check that pill before you sign anything off.

steps.title: Which screen owns which job
steps.instruction: Two different areas are involved, and only one of them is yours. Match each job to the screen that does it.

pairs.left: Switch Protect personal data on for the whole organisation
pairs.right: Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield, tab Overview
pairs.note: The master switch lives on Overview, and it is what makes the four numbered steps clickable.

pairs.left: Tick the kinds of personal data to look for, and set How strict
pairs.right: Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield, step What we look for
pairs.note: Same page, step 1. How strict sits above the table of 21 kinds.

pairs.left: Read the evidence of what was hidden, and where data went
pairs.right: Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield, tab What happened
pairs.note: The evidence tab. It stays readable even while the master switch is off.

pairs.left: Install or restart the detection service
pairs.note: A different area with a different owner: the person who runs the server, not the organisation admin. Enterprise installs only. The Privacy Shield page shows the status in its header, but the fix happens here.

steps.title: The first configuration, in order
steps.instruction: Drag the six steps of a first switch-on into the order the Privacy Shield page walks you through them.

items.label: On Overview, switch Protect personal data on
Tick the kinds of personal data that matter for your work
On What we look for, set How strict — Balanced is the tested setting
On When we find something, choose placeholders or Do not send the message
Press Save changes and wait for Saved successfully!
Back on Overview, read How things stand

sim.feedback: The switch comes first: it is what makes the other steps clickable at all. Then work down What we look for as it is laid out, with How strict above the table of kinds, and Balanced is the level every kind of data was tuned and measured at. Nothing is in force until Save changes, and Overview is where you read back what you just decided.

steps.question: A works council member at Van Dijk Groep asks where the checking happens. Which answer is correct?

choices.label: A service on your organisation's own server reads the message before it goes to the AI; nothing is sent elsewhere to be checked.
The AI provider sees the message first and flags the personal data, so Bee Flow can strip it from the answer.
choices.feedback: That would defeat the purpose: the provider has already seen the personal data. The check runs before the message leaves, not after.

choices.label: The text goes to an outside scanning service, which sends the findings back.
choices.feedback: Nothing is sent elsewhere to be checked. The detection service runs on your own server, which is exactly why the feature can be promised under GDPR.

choices.label: Only your own lists of words and fixed formats under Your own data are ever matched; no detection model is involved.
choices.feedback: That is what you are left with when the detection service is missing: your own words and patterns still match, but none of the 21 categories are detected.

steps.explanation: The detection service runs on your own server. It reads the message before it is sent, finds what the ticked categories describe, and the text never leaves the organisation for that check. When the service is absent, only your own lists of words and fixed formats still fire.

steps.title: Turn it on, with a first set of categories
steps.instruction: Open Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield and switch Protect personal data on. On What we look for, set How strict to Balanced and tick the kinds that match your work — for a purchasing team like Van Dijk Groep's, at least Person Names, Email Addresses, Phone Numbers, IBAN Numbers and Company names. Press Save changes, then check that Overview no longer shows Kinds of data at 0 of 21.

steps.title: What you can do now, and two gaps
steps.bodyMd:
**What you can do now**

- Switch the shield on for your organisation and read How things stand, card by card, as a summary of your own decisions.
- Say what an empty category list really does, which is the widest scan rather than a safe one, and what a detection service that is not running does. The header pill on the Privacy Shield page tells you; the server-operator console at Admin → Security → Guardrails is where it is fixed.
- Explain that nothing is in force until Save changes reports *Saved successfully!*

**Two gaps to write down**

1. The 21 categories are generic. Van Dijk Groep's own contract-number format is not among them, and neither are the supplier names the AI needs to keep reading. That is the next chapter: *What we look for* and *Your own data*.
2. **One last check before an outside AI** is still off, so an external model is covered only by the always-on check you just configured.

practiceTopic.title: Switching on the Organisation Privacy Shield
practiceTopic.summary: How an org admin enables the Privacy Shield, and the two configurations that look finished but catch nothing.
facts: The Privacy Shield lives under Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield: Overview, the numbered steps What we look for, Your own data, When we find something and Leaving your org, then What happened; Admin → Security → Guardrails is a separate area with a separate owner.
The master switch is called Protect personal data; it is off for a new organisation, and the four numbered steps stay inactive until it is on.
The catalogue holds 21 kinds of personal data, and Overview's What we look for card shows how many are ticked in the row Kinds of data, as "n of 21".

An empty category list is read as "no narrowing", so the detector is asked about every kind it knows, while Overview still lists "No kinds of data are selected" on its review card and shows Kinds of data at "0 of 21" in amber.
The three strictness presets are Low sensitivity, Balanced and High sensitivity; Balanced carries the Recommended badge and is the level every quality number was measured at.

Detection runs on a service on your own server; the text is not sent elsewhere to be checked. The page header shows Detection running, or a red Detection service not installed / not responding, and the fix happens in Admin → Security → Guardrails.
Changes only take effect after pressing Save changes in the save bar, which confirms with the toast Saved successfully!
Overview states that org rules run before any agent's own rules: agents can be stricter, never looser.

actionChecks.label: Shield on with at least one category
actionChecks.hint: In Settings → Organisation → Privacy Shield: switch Protect personal data on, tick at least one kind of personal data on What we look for, then press Save changes.

endpoints.returns: the saved shield config object for the learners own organisation (any member may read it): enabled (bool), piiDetectionCategories (array of category names), piiDetectionConfidenceThreshold, piiDetectionAction, updatedAt, updatedBy

criteria.label: The shield is switched on and saved
criteria.hint: Overview → Protect personal data must be on, and you must press Save changes — the check reads the saved organisation setting, not the switch on screen.
criteria.rule: GET /api/org-privacy-shield/:orgid → enabled === true (the org id is filled in for you; a never-saved org answers enabled: false)

criteria.label: At least one kind of personal data is ticked
criteria.hint: What we look for → tick the kinds that matter for your work, then Save changes. Overview must no longer show Kinds of data at 0 of 21.
criteria.rule: GET /api/org-privacy-shield/:orgid → piiDetectionCategories is a non-empty array of category names
